## Verdict

Acme Desk costs least for a team of 35, at $280 per month. Its 10-seat minimum sits well below the team size, so all 35 seats bill at the list rate of $8. Kelp is the most expensive at $850 despite only 35 people needing access, because its 50-seat minimum forces payment for 15 seats the team will not use.

## Vendors

| Vendor | Price per seat | Minimum seats |
|---|---|---|
| Acme Desk | $8 | 10 |
| Fennel HQ | $12 | 25 |
| Kelp | $17 | 50 |

## Cost at this size

Seats paid for is the team size (35) or the vendor minimum, whichever is larger.

- **Acme Desk:** minimum 10 is below 35, so 35 seats paid. 35 × $8 = **$280 per month**.
- **Fennel HQ:** minimum 25 is below 35, so 35 seats paid. 35 × $12 = **$420 per month**.
- **Kelp:** minimum 50 exceeds 35, so 50 seats paid. 50 × $17 = **$850 per month**. Effective rate $24.29 per person ($850 ÷ 35).

Acme Desk is $140 per month cheaper than Fennel HQ and $570 cheaper than Kelp — $1,680 and $6,840 over twelve months.

## Risks

Acme Desk and Fennel HQ both scale linearly from here, so the $140 monthly gap widens as the team grows. Kelp's $850 is fixed until 50 people, at which point its effective rate drops to $17 against Acme Desk's $400 — Acme Desk still leads on list price at every size above its minimum.

This is a price comparison and nothing more. The list gives per-seat rates and seat minimums only, with no detail on features, support tiers, usage limits, or security posture, so a cheaper seat may buy a smaller product.

All figures assume monthly billing as stated. Annual commitments, volume discounts, onboarding fees, and migration costs are absent from the price list and could reorder the result. Worth confirming whether minimums bind at signup or only at renewal.
